summary: Undyed cut-pile velvet, a soft ivory pile with a bright sheen at the edges, as on cushions, drapes and evening wear; tint it any colour.
_comment: Undyed cut-pile velvet (Phase11 wish list). A dense pile of short cut fibre ends stands on a buried ground weave, so the face shows no threads, only a fine stipple of tuft tips, and its look is the pile's sheen at grazing angles. OPAQUE with full FUZZ (the most of any textile; Felt 0.9) and a lower fuzz roughness than felt, so the sheen gathers at the silhouette as velvet's does. Authored at an undyed ivory so a Creator's tint reaches the dyed colours below it; the fuzz colour is a constant the tint does not reach. Lane L2: ambientCG has no velvet scan at a scale option's size. Layers: Pilling01 (damage), Creases01 (crushed fold lines), Dust01 (a deposit), under Grime01 (an older mask: the row's order kept).
name: Velvet_Natural_Clean_Base_s001_v01

sources.why: Colour: undyed cotton or silk pile, an ivory (linear 0.40, 0.36, 0.29 face-on; no measured value; Physically Based has no fabric entries), well darker than Canvas or Felt because a deep pile traps light face-on: the sheen at the edges is what reads as ivory, and at 0.55 it had nothing to stand out against (rig run 1 read as matte plaster). IOR 1.53: cellulose. Roughness ~0.67 in the map. Fuzz 1.0, colour 0.92, 0.89, 0.82, roughness 0.3: velvet's look is its pile's grazing-angle sheen, stronger and tighter than felt's (0.9, 0.7).
